description: HIPAA regulation knowledge base: Privacy Rule (45 CFR Part 164 Subpart E), Security Rule (Subpart C), and Breach Notification Rule (Subpart D). Each entry is a requirement a covered entity's policies and procedures are expected to address.

requirements.title: Security Management Process
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

requirements.title: Risk Analysis
requirements.summary: Conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI held by the organization.

requirements.title: Risk Management
requirements.summary: Implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.

requirements.title: Sanction Policy
requirements.summary: Apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures of the organization.

requirements.title: Information System Activity Review
requirements.summary: Implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.

requirements.title: Assigned Security Responsibility (Security Officer)
requirements.summary: Identify the security official responsible for the development and implementation of the security policies and procedures.

requirements.title: Workforce Security
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures to ensure that all workforce members have appropriate access to ePHI and to prevent those who should not have access from obtaining it.

requirements.title: Authorization and/or Supervision
requirements.summary: Implement procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with ePHI or in locations where it might be accessed.

requirements.title: Workforce Clearance Procedure
requirements.summary: Implement procedures to determine that the access of a workforce member to ePHI is appropriate (e.g., background checks, role review before granting access).

requirements.title: Termination Procedures
requirements.summary: Implement procedures for terminating access to ePHI when employment or association ends, or when access is no longer appropriate.

requirements.title: Information Access Management
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to ePHI that are consistent with the Privacy Rule.

requirements.title: Access Authorization
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures for granting access to ePHI, for example through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism.

requirements.title: Access Establishment and Modification
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures that, based upon the access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify a user's right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.

requirements.title: Security Awareness and Training
requirements.summary: Implement a security awareness and training program for all members of the workforce, including management.

requirements.title: Security Reminders
requirements.summary: Provide periodic security updates and reminders to the workforce.

requirements.title: Protection from Malicious Software
requirements.summary: Implement procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software.

requirements.title: Log-in Monitoring
requirements.summary: Implement procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies.

requirements.title: Password Management
requirements.summary: Implement procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords.

requirements.title: Security Incident Procedures
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures to address security incidents.

requirements.title: Incident Response and Reporting
requirements.summary: Identify and respond to suspected or known security incidents; mitigate, to the extent practicable, harmful effects of security incidents that are known; and document security incidents and their outcomes.

requirements.title: Contingency Plan
requirements.summary: Establish (and implement as needed) policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (e.g., fire, vandalism, system failure, natural disaster) that damages systems containing ePHI.

requirements.title: Data Backup Plan
requirements.summary: Establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of ePHI.

requirements.title: Disaster Recovery Plan
requirements.summary: Establish (and implement as needed) procedures to restore any loss of data.

requirements.title: Emergency Mode Operation Plan
requirements.summary: Establish (and implement as needed) procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for protection of the security of ePHI while operating in emergency mode.

requirements.title: Testing and Revision Procedures
requirements.summary: Implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans.

requirements.title: Applications and Data Criticality Analysis
requirements.summary: Assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components.

requirements.title: Evaluation
requirements.summary: Perform periodic technical and nontechnical evaluations that establish the extent to which security policies and procedures meet the requirements of the Security Rule, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of ePHI.

requirements.title: Business Associate Contracts and Other Arrangements
requirements.summary: A covered entity may permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI on its behalf only if satisfactory assurances are obtained, in accordance with 164.314(a), that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information.

requirements.title: Facility Access Controls
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems and the facilities in which they are housed, while ensuring that properly authorized access is allowed.

requirements.title: Contingency Operations (Facility)
requirements.summary: Establish (and implement as needed) procedures that allow facility access in support of restoration of lost data under the disaster recovery plan and emergency mode operations plan.

requirements.title: Facility Security Plan
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft.

requirements.title: Access Control and Validation Procedures
requirements.summary: Implement procedures to control and validate a person's access to facilities based on their role or function, including visitor control and control of access to software programs for testing and revision.

requirements.title: Maintenance Records
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures to document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility related to security (e.g., hardware, walls, doors, locks).

requirements.title: Workstation Use
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access ePHI.

requirements.title: Workstation Security
requirements.summary: Implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access ePHI to restrict access to authorized users.

requirements.title: Device and Media Controls
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures that govern the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media that contain ePHI into and out of a facility, and the movement of these items within the facility.

requirements.title: Media Disposal
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures to address the final disposition of ePHI and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored.

requirements.title: Media Re-use
requirements.summary: Implement procedures for removal of ePHI from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use.

requirements.title: Media Accountability
requirements.summary: Maintain a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and any person responsible therefore.

requirements.title: Data Backup and Storage (Before Movement)
requirements.summary: Create a retrievable, exact copy of ePHI, when needed, before movement of equipment.

requirements.title: Access Control
requirements.summary: Implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain ePHI to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights.

requirements.title: Unique User Identification
requirements.summary: Assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.

requirements.title: Emergency Access Procedure
requirements.summary: Establish (and implement as needed) procedures for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency.

requirements.title: Automatic Logoff
requirements.summary: Implement electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity.

requirements.title: Encryption and Decryption (At Rest)
requirements.summary: Implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt ePHI.

requirements.title: Audit Controls
requirements.summary: Implement hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use ePHI.

requirements.title: Integrity
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures to protect ePHI from improper alteration or destruction.

requirements.title: Mechanism to Authenticate ePHI
requirements.summary: Implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.

requirements.title: Person or Entity Authentication
requirements.summary: Implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.

requirements.title: Transmission Security
requirements.summary: Implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to ePHI that is being transmitted over an electronic communications network.

requirements.title: Integrity Controls (In Transit)
requirements.summary: Implement security measures to ensure that electronically transmitted ePHI is not improperly modified without detection until disposed of.

requirements.title: Encryption (In Transit)
requirements.summary: Implement a mechanism to encrypt ePHI whenever deemed appropriate, particularly during transmission over open networks.

requirements.title: Business Associate Contracts (Content Requirements)
requirements.summary: The contract or other arrangement with a business associate must meet specified requirements: the BA must comply with the Security Rule, ensure subcontractors comply, and report security incidents including breaches of unsecured PHI.

requirements.title: Policies and Procedures
requirements.summary: Implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the standards, implementation specifications, and other requirements of the Security Rule; policies may be changed at any time provided changes are documented and implemented.

requirements.title: Documentation
requirements.summary: Maintain the policies and procedures in written (which may be electronic) form; and if an action, activity, or assessment is required to be documented, maintain a written record of it.

requirements.title: Documentation Retention (6 Years)
requirements.summary: Retain required documentation for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.

requirements.title: Documentation Availability
requirements.summary: Make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.

requirements.title: Documentation Updates
requirements.summary: Review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the ePHI.

requirements.title: Permitted and Required Uses and Disclosures (General Rules)
requirements.summary: A covered entity may not use or disclose PHI except as permitted or required by the Privacy Rule: to the individual, for treatment/payment/health care operations, with authorization, and in other specified circumstances. Disclosure is required to the individual on request and to HHS for compliance investigations.

requirements.title: Minimum Necessary Standard
requirements.summary: When using or disclosing PHI or when requesting PHI from another covered entity, make reasonable efforts to limit PHI to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose. Does not apply to treatment disclosures, disclosures to the individual, authorized disclosures, or disclosures required by law.

requirements.title: Disclosures to Business Associates (Privacy)
requirements.summary: A covered entity may disclose PHI to a business associate and allow it to create, receive, maintain, or transmit PHI on its behalf only with satisfactory assurance (a business associate agreement) that the BA will appropriately safeguard the information.

requirements.title: Personal Representatives
requirements.summary: Treat a personal representative (a person with authority to act on behalf of an individual, e.g., for minors or incapacitated adults) as the individual for purposes of the Privacy Rule, with exceptions for abuse or endangerment situations.

requirements.title: Business Associate Agreement Content (Privacy)
requirements.summary: Business associate contracts must establish permitted uses/disclosures, prohibit further impermissible use, require safeguards, require breach/incident reporting, ensure subcontractor compliance, provide for access/amendment/accounting support, and require return or destruction of PHI at termination.

requirements.title: Uses and Disclosures for Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations (TPO)
requirements.summary: A covered entity may use or disclose PHI for its own treatment, payment, or health care operations, and in specified circumstances for those of another covered entity, without individual authorization.

requirements.title: Authorizations for Uses and Disclosures
requirements.summary: Uses and disclosures not otherwise permitted require a valid written authorization with core elements (description, who may disclose/receive, purpose, expiration, signature) and required statements (right to revoke, conditioning limits, redisclosure risk). Special rules for psychotherapy notes and marketing; sale of PHI requires authorization.

requirements.title: Facility Directories
requirements.summary: May use limited PHI (name, location, general condition, religious affiliation) in facility directories if the individual is informed and given an opportunity to object; emergency provisions apply.

requirements.title: Disclosures to Family, Friends, and for Notification
requirements.summary: May disclose PHI directly relevant to the involvement of a family member, relative, or close friend in the individual's care or payment, and for notification of location/condition/death, subject to the individual's agreement or, when incapacitated, professional judgment.

requirements.title: Uses and Disclosures Not Requiring Authorization or Opportunity to Object
requirements.summary: Permits uses and disclosures without authorization for: as required by law; public health activities; victims of abuse/neglect/domestic violence; health oversight; judicial and administrative proceedings; law enforcement; decedents (coroners, funeral directors); organ donation; research (with waiver or other conditions); serious threat to health or safety; specialized government functions; and workers' compensation.

requirements.title: De-identification of PHI
requirements.summary: Health information is not PHI if de-identified via expert determination or the safe harbor method (removal of 18 identifiers with no actual knowledge of re-identifiability); re-identification codes must be protected.

requirements.title: Minimum Necessary Implementation (Role-Based)
requirements.summary: Identify workforce members or classes who need access to PHI to carry out their duties, the categories of PHI needed, and conditions appropriate to such access; implement policies limiting routine and non-routine disclosures and requests accordingly.

requirements.title: Limited Data Sets and Data Use Agreements
requirements.summary: May use or disclose a limited data set (with specified direct identifiers removed) for research, public health, or health care operations only with a data use agreement.

requirements.title: Verification of Identity and Authority
requirements.summary: Prior to disclosure, verify the identity of a person requesting PHI and the authority of the person to have access to it, if not known; obtain any required documentation, statements, or representations.

requirements.title: Notice of Privacy Practices (NPP)
requirements.summary: Individuals have a right to adequate notice of the uses and disclosures of PHI that may be made and of their rights and the covered entity's legal duties. The notice must contain specified elements, be provided at first service delivery, be posted, be available on any website, and providers with direct treatment relationships must make a good-faith effort to obtain written acknowledgment of receipt.

requirements.title: Right to Request Restrictions
requirements.summary: Individuals may request restrictions on uses and disclosures of PHI for TPO and to persons involved in care. The covered entity is not required to agree except it MUST agree to restrict disclosure to a health plan when the disclosure is for payment/operations and pertains to an item or service paid in full out of pocket.

requirements.title: Confidential Communications
requirements.summary: Health care providers must permit individuals to request and must accommodate reasonable requests to receive communications of PHI by alternative means or at alternative locations.

requirements.title: Right of Access to PHI
requirements.summary: Individuals have a right to inspect and obtain a copy of their PHI in a designated record set, generally within 30 days (one 30-day extension permitted), in the form and format requested if readily producible (including electronic copies), with only a reasonable cost-based fee; limited grounds for denial, some reviewable.

requirements.title: Right to Amend PHI
requirements.summary: Individuals have the right to have a covered entity amend PHI in a designated record set; the entity must act within 60 days (one 30-day extension), may deny on specified grounds, and must permit a statement of disagreement and provide the amendment or disagreement with future disclosures.

requirements.title: Accounting of Disclosures
requirements.summary: Individuals have a right to an accounting of disclosures of PHI made in the six years prior to the request, excluding TPO, to the individual, authorized, directory, and certain other disclosures; response within 60 days; first accounting in any 12-month period must be free.

requirements.title: Privacy Officer and Contact Person
requirements.summary: Designate a privacy official responsible for the development and implementation of privacy policies and procedures, and a contact person or office responsible for receiving complaints and providing information about the notice.

requirements.title: Privacy Training
requirements.summary: Train all members of the workforce on privacy policies and procedures as necessary and appropriate for their functions: for new members within a reasonable time after joining, and after material changes to policies; document the training.

requirements.title: Safeguards (Privacy)
requirements.summary: Have in place appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect the privacy of PHI in any form (including oral and paper), reasonably safeguarding PHI from any intentional or unintentional use or disclosure in violation of the Privacy Rule and limiting incidental uses and disclosures.

requirements.title: Complaints Process
requirements.summary: Provide a process for individuals to make complaints concerning the covered entity's privacy policies and procedures or its compliance with them; document all complaints received and their disposition.

requirements.title: Sanctions (Privacy)
requirements.summary: Have and apply appropriate sanctions against members of the workforce who fail to comply with the privacy policies and procedures or the Privacy Rule; document sanctions applied.

requirements.title: Mitigation
requirements.summary: Mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect known to the covered entity of a use or disclosure of PHI in violation of its policies or the Privacy Rule by the entity or its business associates.

requirements.title: Refraining from Intimidating or Retaliatory Acts
requirements.summary: May not intimidate, threaten, coerce, discriminate against, or take other retaliatory action against individuals for exercising their rights, filing complaints, participating in investigations, or opposing unlawful acts.

requirements.title: No Waiver of Rights
requirements.summary: May not require individuals to waive their rights under the Privacy Rule or their right to file a complaint with HHS as a condition of treatment, payment, enrollment, or eligibility for benefits.

requirements.title: Privacy Policies and Procedures
requirements.summary: Implement policies and procedures with respect to PHI designed to comply with the Privacy Rule and Breach Notification Rule; change policies promptly to reflect changes in law; document and implement changes consistently with the notice.

requirements.title: Privacy Documentation and Retention
requirements.summary: Maintain privacy policies and procedures, communications, and required documentation in written or electronic form for 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later.

requirements.title: Breach Definition and Risk Assessment
requirements.summary: An impermissible acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of unsecured PHI is presumed to be a breach unless the entity demonstrates a low probability of compromise via a documented risk assessment considering at least: nature and extent of PHI, the unauthorized person, whether PHI was actually acquired or viewed, and the extent of mitigation.

requirements.title: Notification to Individuals
requirements.summary: Following discovery of a breach of unsecured PHI, notify each affected individual without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; written notice with specified content (what happened, types of information, steps individuals should take, what the entity is doing, contact procedures); substitute notice provisions when contact information is insufficient.

requirements.title: Notification to the Media
requirements.summary: For a breach involving more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction, notify prominent media outlets serving that area without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery.

requirements.title: Notification to HHS
requirements.summary: Notify the Secretary of HHS of breaches of unsecured PHI: contemporaneously with individual notice for breaches involving 500 or more individuals; annually (within 60 days after calendar year end) for smaller breaches via a maintained log.

requirements.title: Notification by Business Associates
requirements.summary: A business associate must notify the covered entity of a breach of unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery, identifying affected individuals and providing available details.

requirements.title: Breach Administrative Requirements and Burden of Proof
requirements.summary: Comply with administrative requirements (training, complaints, sanctions, documentation) with respect to breach notification; the covered entity or BA bears the burden of demonstrating that required notifications were made or that the incident did not constitute a breach.
